faults.note: Screen 4 and the explanation say the angle to the normal 'changes by the same amount on the way in and again on the way out', so the beam turns twice as far. That leaves him to see why two changes in angle to a moving normal add to a turn of the beam. Give the step he can check: the angle between the arriving and leaving beams is the two equal angles together, so when each changes by 10° the gap changes by 20°, and with the torch still the leaving beam turns 20°. The explanation's periscope sentence says each mirror turns the light 90° without the reason (arrives and leaves at 45° to the normal).

'Light travels in straight lines' is false at the boundary the next idea teaches; say 'through air'. 'Real mirrors ... are never perfectly flat' reads as a sweeping never; 'are not perfectly flat' is enough. The analogy's 'a pool player aims at the pocket's mirror copy' claims what all players do; make it one way to aim.

faults.fault: interactive brief shows only the effect
faults.note: The brief names the cause (equal angles at the mirror) and the effect (the dashed line back ending at one image) under one action, the eye's drag. The eye dragged past the mirror's end is the setting where no reflected light arrives and no image is seen.
